patients.summary: Healthy high school math teacher who joined in 2022. Develops a heliotrope rash and proximal weakness in 2024; dermatology makes a clinical diagnosis of dermatomyositis, rheumatology confirms it in January 2026 (anti-Mi-2, EMG, biopsy) and starts prednisone and methotrexate.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
51 y/o woman establishing care. Prior PCP retired; records requested.

No active complaints. Feels well, walks most evenings, gardens. No chronic conditions and no daily medications.

PMH: none.
PSH: lap cholecystectomy 2014; tubal ligation 1999.
Meds: none.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother - autoimmune thyroiditis; father - hypertension; maternal aunt - rheumatoid arthritis.
SH: teaches high school math. Never smoker. Wine 1-2 glasses a week. No drugs.

ROS: negative except as above. No fatigue, no weight change, no joint pain, no rash.

Exam: Well appearing. HEENT normal. Thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, healed lap scars. Skin without rash. Strength 5/5 throughout. No edema.

PHQ-2 = 0.

Assessment/Plan:
1. Adult preventive care. Screening labs: CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH (mother's thyroid history), A1c. One-time hep C and HIV screen, she agrees.
2. Immunizations: no record of a tetanus booster in 10+ years - Tdap given today. Flu and COVID in the fall. Discussed Shingrix series, she'd like to start after the school year settles.
3. Cancer screening: per her, colonoscopy last year and a mammogram last year were both fine; Pap 2 years ago. Will confirm from records.
4. RTC 1 year, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Heather - all of your bloodwork from Wednesday came back normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, thyroid, sugar (A1c), and cholesterol all in good ranges. Hep C and HIV screens negative. Nothing to change. Enjoy the rest of the summer.

Reviewed and abstracted to chart. HM updated.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison: 10/2021 outside study. Breast density: scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, architectural distortion or calcifications in either breast. Skin and nipples unremarkable.

documents.title: Rash and feeling weak
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, school just ended and I finally have time to deal with this. For maybe two months I've had a purplish-red color on my upper eyelids and some red blotchy patches on the backs of my hands. I thought it was a reaction to a new eye cream but I stopped it and nothing changed. The other thing - and maybe unrelated - stairs have been a real effort since the winter, and holding my arms up to blow-dry or comb my hair wears me out. I'm not sick otherwise. Could I come in next week?

orders.reason: eyelid and dorsal hand rash with proximal weakness

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: 53F, last seen 8/2023 for physical. About 2 months of violet-red discoloration of both upper lids and red patches on the backs of both hands. Not itchy to speak of. Stopped a new eye cream, no change. Separately, since roughly winter, climbing the stairs to her 2nd-floor classroom takes effort and her arms tire holding a hair dryer or comb. No muscle pain, no trouble swallowing, no shortness of breath. Denies fever, weight loss, night sweats. No new meds or supplements.

O: Afebrile, vitals reviewed. Violaceous discoloration of the upper eyelids bilaterally. Blanching erythematous patches over the dorsal hands. Joints without synovitis. Strength 4+/5 deltoids and hip flexors bilaterally, symmetric; distal strength 5/5. Reflexes 2+ and symmetric. Heart and lungs normal.

A/P: Rash of the lids and hands with symmetric proximal weakness - concerned for an inflammatory myopathy such as dermatomyositis.
- CK, ANA, CMP, CBC, TSH today.
- Dermatology referral for the rash; asked their office to see her this summer.
- Will call with results. If swallowing or breathing trouble, call right away.

documents.title: Results from Monday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Heather - your CK, a muscle enzyme, is high at 1,840, and the ANA (an autoimmune screening test) is positive at 1:640. Two liver tests are mildly up, which goes along with muscle inflammation rather than a liver problem. Thyroid and blood counts are normal. Together with the rash and the weakness this fits an inflammatory muscle condition, most likely dermatomyositis. Dermatology has you on July 19; I've sent them these results. We'll talk after that visit.

documents.title: RE: Results from Monday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you for explaining. I looked it up and it sounds scary but I'll wait to hear what they say. See you after the 19th.

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE DERMATOLOGY GROUP - CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 07/19/2024
Re: Heather Fournier, DOB 10/25/1970

Thank you for asking us to see this 53-year-old teacher. Over several months she has found it steadily harder to get up stairs and to keep her arms raised to comb her hair, and more recently noticed red skin changes on the face and hands. No fevers, no weight loss.

PSH: cholecystectomy, tubal ligation. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Family: mother with autoimmune thyroiditis; maternal aunt with rheumatoid arthritis; father with hypertension.
Social: never smoker, a glass or two of wine weekly, high school math teacher.

Vitals: T 36.8 C (98.2 F), BP 124/76, P 80, RR 14, SpO2 99% RA.

Exam: Violaceous erythema of both upper eyelids (heliotrope pattern). Erythematous macules and thin patches on the dorsal hands. Scalp, trunk and nails otherwise unremarkable. Symmetric weakness of proximal arm and leg muscles on confrontation.

Data: Labs drawn by her primary care office on 06/24 - creatine kinase 1,840 U/L and ANA positive (1:640, speckled).

Impression: Heliotrope eruption with hand involvement, symmetric proximal weakness and a raised CK - clinically dermatomyositis.

Recommendations:
1. Rheumatology for confirmation (myositis antibodies, EMG/biopsy as they see fit) and systemic treatment.
2. Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen and sun-protective clothing; the eruption is often photosensitive.
3. We are glad to see her again for the skin as needed.

cc: primary care physician

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, she is at home; verified name and DOB.

Reviewed the dermatology letter with her. Their read is dermatomyositis on clinical grounds. She says the lids look about the same, hands a little less red with sunscreen. Stairs still slow. Swallowing fine, no breathing complaints.

A/P: Dermatomyositis, clinical diagnosis - added to problem list.
- Rheumatology referral placed today for confirmation and treatment.
- Explained why confirming matters and that treatment is usually steroids plus a second medicine.
- She will call if weakness worsens quickly, or with choking or breathlessness.

documents.body:
Physical; last full exam 8/2023. Dermatomyositis (clinical dx by derm 7/2024), never made it to rheumatology - the October appointment was cancelled and not rebooked.

She says the weakness held steady through the year, but since early summer stairs are harder again and she rests partway up. Lifting her arms to put things on high shelves is tiring. Lids still dusky, knuckles red. No dysphagia, no dyspnea, no fevers.

Meds: none. NKDA.

Exam: Well appearing. Violaceous upper-lid discoloration. Erythematous patches over the knuckles. Heart regular, lungs clear, abdomen benign. Strength 4+/5 shoulder abductors and hip flexors bilaterally, 5/5 distally. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal, Pap/HPV collected. Breasts without mass.

PHQ-9 = 2.

A/P:
1. Dermatomyositis, with weakness worse this summer. CK today. New rheumatology referral, asked for an early slot; she has agreed to take the time off this time.
2. Preventive: Pap/HPV today. Labs CBC, CMP, lipids, A1c, TSH. Mammogram due in fall - order in. Colonoscopy not due until 2031. Flu/COVID in October.
3. RTC after rheumatology.

documents.title: Lab results and rheumatology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Heather, your CK came back at 2,650 - higher than last summer's 1,840, which matches the weakness you've noticed. The liver tests are mildly up again from the muscle. Everything else (blood counts, kidney, sugar, cholesterol, thyroid) is fine. Rheumatology has your referral marked as soon; their scheduler should call this week. The Pap result will follow in a few days.

documents.title: Rheumatology Consultation
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
RHEUMATOLOGY - NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Seen 11/19/2025. Referred by her primary care physician.

Ms. Fournier is a 55-year-old math teacher with a heliotrope eruption, red knuckle patches and proximal weakness. Dermatology diagnosed dermatomyositis clinically in July 2024 (CK 1,840, ANA 1:640 speckled). She deferred the first rheumatology visit. Weakness was stable for about a year, then progressed from early summer 2025 (CK 2,650 in August). Now rests halfway up a flight of stairs. No dysphagia, dyspnea, cough, fevers or joint swelling.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: Heliotrope discoloration of the lids; scaly erythematous patches over the MCP and PIP joints. Proximal muscle weakness, symmetric, upper and lower limbs (deltoids and hip flexors 4/5). Distal strength full. Lungs clear. No synovitis.

Today: CK 3,120 U/L; AST 96, ALT 71 (muscle source likely).

Impression: Probable dermatomyositis, progressing.

Plan:
1. Myositis-specific and associated antibody panel.
2. EMG/NCS - requested at our neurophysiology lab.
3. Muscle biopsy guided by the EMG, contralateral side.
4. Return after results to discuss treatment.

cc: PCP

reports.text: Nerve conduction: right median, ulnar, peroneal and sural nerves with normal distal latencies, amplitudes and conduction velocities; F-waves normal. Needle EMG: right deltoid, biceps, iliopsoas and vastus lateralis show fibrillation potentials and positive sharp waves, with early recruitment of short-duration, low-amplitude, polyphasic motor unit potentials. Right first dorsal interosseous and tibialis anterior normal. Thoracic paraspinals not sampled.
reports.conclusion: Irritable myopathy affecting proximal muscles of the right arm and leg, with normal nerve conduction. Consistent with an inflammatory myopathy. Left vastus lateralis suggested for biopsy.

procedures.procedure: Nerve conduction study with needle EMG

reports.text: Specimen: skeletal muscle, left vastus lateralis, open biopsy (fresh and fixed portions). Frozen and paraffin sections show perifascicular atrophy, with small, basophilic fibers concentrated at the edges of fascicles. Perivascular inflammatory infiltrates in the perimysium, predominantly lymphocytes. Scattered necrotic and regenerating fibers. No rimmed vacuoles, no inclusions. Special stains and enzyme histochemistry otherwise unremarkable for this pattern.
reports.conclusion: Inflammatory myopathy with perifascicular atrophy and perivascular inflammation, consistent with dermatomyositis.

medications.sig: Take 3 tablets (60 mg) by mouth every morning
Take 6 tablets (15 mg) by mouth once a week on the same day
Take 1 tablet (1000 units) by mouth daily

documents.title: Rheumatology Follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
RHEUMATOLOGY FOLLOW-UP - 01/21/2026

She returns to go over the workup for the problem first evaluated by dermatology in July 2024. Over the last six months she has had more trouble with stairs and with lifting her arms; brushing her hair now tires her out, and she notices her neck feels weak holding her head up while sitting. No dysphagia or dyspnea. No regular medications. NKDA.

PSH: cholecystectomy 2014, tubal ligation 1999.
FH: mother - autoimmune thyroiditis; maternal aunt - rheumatoid arthritis; father - hypertension.
SH: high school math teacher; never smoked; wine 1-2 glasses a week.

Exam: Symmetric proximal weakness in arms and legs; neck flexors 4/5. Violaceous rash of the eyelids. Scaly red patches over the knuckles. Lungs clear.

Results:
- CK 3,480 U/L today (3,120 in November). AST 104, ALT 78.
- Myositis panel: anti-Mi-2 positive; remaining myositis-specific antibodies negative.
- EMG 12/10: irritable myopathy, proximal.
- Muscle biopsy (L vastus lateralis) 01/06: perifascicular atrophy with perivascular inflammation - consistent with dermatomyositis.
- Pre-treatment screening: HBsAg nonreactive, HCV Ab nonreactive, QuantiFERON negative.

Assessment: Dermatomyositis, confirmed by antibody, electrodiagnostic and biopsy findings.

Plan:
1. Prednisone 60 mg each morning. Will taper by response.
2. Methotrexate 15 mg once weekly, folic acid 1 mg daily. No alcohol beyond an occasional glass. CBC and liver tests every 4-6 weeks at first.
3. Vitamin D3 1000 units daily; calcium through diet.
4. CT chest, abdomen and pelvis for age-appropriate malignancy screening in adult dermatomyositis; her mammogram, Pap and colonoscopy are current.
5. Please consider bone density and pneumococcal vaccination with her PCP.
6. Return in 8 weeks.

cc: PCP

documents.title: Update from rheumatology
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi - rheumatology confirmed the dermatomyositis. I started prednisone 60 mg yesterday and the methotrexate this Sunday, plus folic acid and vitamin D. They said you might want to do a bone scan and a pneumonia vaccine. CT scan is booked for Feb 4. Should I come in?

documents.title: RE: Update from rheumatology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the update, glad you have a plan. Yes - let's see you after the CT. The front desk will offer Feb 11. We'll give the pneumonia vaccine then and order the bone density test. Prednisone can raise blood sugar, so we'll check it at the visit.

reports.text: CT of the chest with IV contrast, performed with the abdomen and pelvis. Lungs are clear without nodules, consolidation, ground-glass or reticular opacity. No interstitial lung disease. Airways patent. No pleural or pericardial effusion. Heart size normal. No mediastinal, hilar or axillary lymphadenopathy. Thyroid and visualized breast tissue unremarkable. No osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: Normal CT chest. No mass, adenopathy or interstitial lung disease.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Liver, spleen, pancreas, adrenal glands and kidneys normal in appearance. Gallbladder surgically absent; no biliary dilatation. Bowel normal in caliber without wall thickening or mass. Uterus and adnexa unremarkable for age. No ascites. No retroperitoneal, mesenteric or pelvic lymphadenopathy. Bones without suspicious lesion.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of malignancy in the abdomen or pelvis. Post-cholecystectomy.

orders.order: DXA bone density, hip and spine

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to catch up after rheumatology. Dermatomyositis now confirmed (anti-Mi-2 positive, myopathic EMG, biopsy with perifascicular atrophy). Three weeks into prednisone 60 mg daily; methotrexate 15 mg weekly with folic acid and vitamin D3 1000 units.

Says the stairs feel a bit easier already. Took methotrexate the last 3 Sundays without nausea. CT last week normal - she had read the report and was relieved.

Exam: BP 126/80. Weight up about 1.5 kg. Lids still dusky. Strength in the hip flexors 4/5, shoulders 4+/5. Lungs clear.

A/P:
1. Dermatomyositis - treatment per rheumatology. Reviewed weekly (not daily) methotrexate dosing; she has a pill box marked for Sundays.
2. Glucocorticoid therapy - BMP for glucose today. DXA ordered. Vitamin D on board, dietary calcium ok (yogurt, milk).
3. Immunosuppressed - PCV20 given today. Flu and COVID already this season. Shingrix complete (2023). No live vaccines.
4. Follow up in summer, or sooner.

reports.study: DXA bone density, hip and spine
reports.text: Dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry of the lumbar spine (L1-L4) and left hip. All vertebral levels evaluable. Lumbar spine T-score -0.9. Total hip T-score -0.4. Indication: long-term glucocorticoid therapy.

documents.title: Bone density result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news - your bone density is normal (spine -0.9, hip -0.4). Keep up the vitamin D and calcium from food. We'll repeat it in a couple of years if you're still on prednisone. Your sugar on the 11th was fine too.

medications.sig: Take 3 tablets (60 mg) by mouth every morning
Take 2 tablets (40 mg) by mouth every morning

Dermatomyositis (anti-Mi-2), 8 weeks into treatment. Clear improvement: climbs her classroom stairs without stopping, can hold her arms up to wash her hair. Lid and knuckle redness fading. Neck no longer feels weak. Methotrexate tolerated, no mouth sores.

Exam: deltoids and hip flexors 4+/5, neck flexors 5/5. Faint heliotrope.

Labs: CK 910 (from 3,480). AST 40, ALT 38. CBC fine.

Plan: Prednisone down to 40 mg daily. Methotrexate 15 mg weekly unchanged with folic acid. Labs again in 4-6 weeks. Return in 8 weeks.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Summer check-in. Dermatomyositis much improved - she finished the school year without trouble on the stairs and is gardening again. On prednisone 20 mg daily since mid-May, methotrexate 15 mg Sundays, folic acid, D3. No mouth sores, no cough, no breathlessness. A few pounds up on prednisone.

Exam: BP 128/80. Wt 71.5 kg. Lids nearly clear, knuckles faint pink. Strength 5-/5 hip flexors, otherwise 5/5. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P:
1. Dermatomyositis, responding. CK, CMP, CBC today (also covers rheum's monitoring labs this cycle - will forward).
2. Prednisone effects - A1c today. BP fine. DXA normal in Feb.
3. Health maintenance: flu and COVID in the fall (inactivated only). Mammogram due November.
4. Rheumatology next in August.
